primary_claim: Reproducing Betley et al.'s out-of-context self-awareness result on Gemma 3 12B IT, a single LoRA layer (or even just a trained steering vector, no LoRA needed) is enough to reproduce risky/safe behavior and the model's ability to report its own risk tolerance; steering works at roughly the same layers for behavior and self-awareness questions, suggesting no separate 'awareness mechanism', and risk-conditioned behavioral backdoors also reproduce with a single LoRA/steering vector, though backdoor self-awareness from the original paper does not replicate.

effect.metric: validation accuracy on risky/safe behavior and self-awareness questions
effect.value: LoRA on all layers reaches ~97% val accuracy on risky/safe behavior; single-layer LoRAs on mid layers (~18-28) do almost as well; awareness-question accuracy is similar but single-layer LoRAs generalize slightly less well; a directly trained layer-22 steering vector achieves even higher validation accuracy than the layer-22 LoRA

contradicts_or_qualifies: unlike the original paper (arXiv:2501.11120), backdoor self-awareness does not replicate: the base and decorrelated models report having a jailbreak as often or more often than the actually jailbroken models, hypothesized to be due to random chance in the original work or Gemma 3 being too small
stated_future_work: study more complex behaviors or larger models to investigate more interesting types of model self-awareness
determine whether luck in fine-tuning outcomes or Gemma 3's smaller size explains the failure to replicate backdoor self-awareness
limitations_stated: backdoor self-awareness does not replicate as in the original paper, and the underlying cause (luck vs. Gemma 3 being too small) is uncertain
the newly trained safety steering vector has only ~0.5 cosine similarity with the vector recovered from LoRA, and its top-similarity tokens are much less interpretable

in the 'investigating further' setup (matching the paper's original training design) validation accuracy is much worse, and the original (non-jailbroken) model reports a jailbreak just as often as jailbroken models
quote: Applying LoRA to a single MLP is enough to reproduce the behavior
